scientific_conclusion: The counterfactual-query-normalized selector converts SFT6's dominant failure regime: on a fresh never-consumed fixture, normalized selection scores 71.1% where raw candidate argmax scores 47.0% — repairing 53 of 79 selection failures. This confirms the candidate-prior-bias hypothesis: the query-conditioned signal is present in the model but raw candidate priors mask it under argmax scoring. The preregistered regression bound (<=3) was exceeded (17 pass->fail): normalization is not strictly dominant — it trades some already-correct selections for many more incorrect ones, net +36. Runtime policy, not training.
caveat_regression_bound: 17 regressions mean normalization changes behavior on ~36% of targets. A production policy would gate the intervention on observed confidence (e.g. adj_top2_margin) — recorded as an open self-model question, not resolved here.
next_research_question: Can a learned self-model predict FROM OBSERVED FEATURES ALONE which targets the normalization helps versus hurts, recovering most of its value while avoiding the 17 regressions?
